title: Merge Intervals
prompt:
Teachers book the school library in time blocks, stored as [start, end] pairs in minutes after 8:00. The front desk wants one clean list of the times the library is busy. Given an array of intervals, merge every group of overlapping intervals and return the merged list sorted by start.

Intervals that only touch also merge: [1, 4] and [4, 5] become [1, 5].

Write mergeIntervals(intervals).

  • mergeIntervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]) returns [[1, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]
  • mergeIntervals([[1, 4], [4, 5]]) returns [[1, 5]]
  • mergeIntervals([[8, 10], [1, 3]]) returns [[1, 3], [8, 10]] (input is not sorted)
  • mergeIntervals([]) returns []

Constraints: 0 to 104 intervals; start <= end; values can be negative. Target: O(n log n).

tests.name: an interval fully inside another
tests.code: assertEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 10], [2, 3], [4, 5]]), [[1, 10]], 'the end must be max(last end, current end), not current end');

tests.name: numbers sort as numbers, not strings
tests.code: assertEqual(mergeIntervals([[10, 12], [9, 9], [100, 101]]), [[9, 9], [10, 12], [100, 101]], 'did you call sort() without a comparator? It sorts "10" before "9".');

hints: Trigger: "overlapping intervals" almost always means sort by start time first. Once sorted, any interval can only overlap the one you merged most recently.
Keep a merged array. For each interval in sorted order: if its start is <= the end of the last merged interval, they overlap, so stretch that end. Otherwise push it as a new block.

Shape:

sorted.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);
for (const current of sorted) {
  const last = merged[merged.length - 1];
  if (last && current[0] <= last[1]) last[1] = Math.max(last[1], current[1]);
  else merged.push(current);
}
explain:
Time O(n log n) for the sort, plus O(n) for the single walk. Space O(n) for the output (and the copy). The sort is what makes the walk work: after sorting, overlaps can only happen between neighbours, so you never compare every pair (which would be O(n²)).

Say it: "Intervals, so I'll sort by start. Then one pass: if the next start is at or before the current end, extend the end with a max; otherwise start a new block. O(n log n) for the sort, O(n) extra space."
